# Anchored Match Cut

**Cut › Match Cut** · v1.0.0 · 30 frames at 30 fps (10–60)

A hard cut that lines up a point in the next scene with a point in the old one, then eases the new scene back to its own framing.

[Preview video](https://github.com/GTKottman/remotion-transitions/releases/download/media/match-cut-anchor@1.0.0.mp4)

## Where it is used

- Match cuts on shape or position
- Object continuity between shots
- Graphic match cuts

## Use it

```tsx
import { linearTiming, TransitionSeries } from '@remotion/transitions';
import { toPresentation } from './src/core';
import matchCutAnchor from './transitions/01-cut/match-cut/match-cut-anchor';

<TransitionSeries.Transition
  presentation={toPresentation(matchCutAnchor, { /* params */ })}
  timing={linearTiming({ durationInFrames: 30 })}
/>
```

Use `linearTiming`: the transition applies its own easing.

## Parameters

| Name | Type | Default | Range | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `fromX` | number | `0.79` | 0–1 | Anchor in scene A, x (0..1). |
| `fromY` | number | `0.5` | 0–1 | Anchor in scene A, y (0..1). |
| `toX` | number | `0.19` | 0–1 | Anchor in scene B, x (0..1). |
| `toY` | number | `0.45` | 0–1 | Anchor in scene B, y (0..1). |
| `scale` | number | `1` | 0.25–4 | Scale of scene B at the cut. |
